Parliament
National Assembly
Complete Verbatim Report of the Proceedings
94
2083 Ashad
Monday
Meeting Number - 21
Presided over by the Chairperson, the meeting commenced at 12:20 PM.
Today's meeting
(12:20 PM)
Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable members, the floor is open for Zero Hour.
First, Honorable Member Chandra Bahadur KC.
Honorable Member Chandra Bahadur KC (Nepali Congress):-
(12:21 PM)
Mr. Chairman, I wish to raise two points. The landless are being evicted, driven away, and harassed. They were promised happiness, but their plight is heartbreaking to witness. Meanwhile, those residing in holding centers are suffering. I request the government to draw its attention to this through you, Mr. Chairman. Simultaneously, on one hand, student unions are being dissolved, and on the other hand, the Rastriya Swatantra Party is inducting around 35,000 youths under 18 years of age into its party. Isn't this a contradiction? Therefore, I wish to draw attention to this as well. I conclude here. Thank you, Jai Nepal.
Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Member Jagat Timilsina.
(12:22 PM)
Honorable Member Jagat Timilsina (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairman,
(12:22 PM)
Nepal's Constitution, the Children Act, the Political Parties Act, and international laws concerning children themselves prohibit a nation that is a signatory to these from giving party membership to individuals under 18 years of age. However, Honorable Chairman, the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party itself has made over 34,000 children under 18 years of age party members, as reported in today's Kantipur Daily. Thus, I draw the attention of the Rastriya Human Rights Commission and other relevant bodies to the defiant behavior of the ruling party, Rastriya Swatantra Party, towards Nepal's Constitution, laws, and international laws, through you, Honorable Chairman. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Member Minasingh Rakhala.
(12:23 PM)
Honorable Member Minasingh Rakhala
(12:23 PM)
(Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Honorable Chairman, first of all, I extend my heartfelt greetings on the occasion of National Paddy Day. Today, Ashad 14th, is National Paddy Day, but this year, due to the irregularity of the monsoon, many farmers have not even been able to sow paddy seeds, let alone transplant them. There is a lack of water in some places, and excessive rain has washed away paddy in others. Due to the inability to transplant on time, production is certain to decrease, directly affecting farmers' income. It is not enough to call it an agricultural country; it is the government's duty to provide timely fertilizer, seeds, irrigation, agricultural insurance, and relief to farmers. If the farmers' pain is ignored, food security itself could be at risk. Therefore, my demand from the government is to immediately assess the affected farmers and provide relief, seeds, irrigation, and necessary agricultural assistance. Only if the farmers survive will the country's economy and food security be strong. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Member Ranjit Karna.
(12:24 PM)
Honorable Member Ranjit Karna (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairman,
(12:24 PM)
In Rajbiraj Municipality of Saptari district, Nepal's "First Planned City," all the city dwellers have been protesting for 43 days. They have not received land ownership certificates for 70 bighas of land and 5,235 households for 85 years. Despite repeated requests, the Government of Nepal has shown no interest. Furthermore, in Ashad 2080 BS, the Land Survey Office even issued a notice stating that land ownership certificates would be distributed, but it was later halted. What's worse is that out of 4,235 households, only 17 people received land ownership certificates. An investigation should be conducted into how these certificates were issued, and they should be distributed to all city dwellers and landowners soon.
Thank you, Jai Nepal.
Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Member Rekha Kumari Jha.
(12:24 PM)
Honorable Member Rekha Kumari Jha
(12:24 PM)
(Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Honorable
Chairman, I wish to draw the government's attention to a serious instance of financial investigation and policy deviation in public administration in this esteemed house. Data has been made public showing the illegal conversion of government vehicles, funded by the state treasury, from white number plates to red number plates for personal use in various public bodies such as the Nepal Drinking Water Corporation, Rajbiraj, Pathari Sanischare Municipality, and some public entities in Kathmandu. While fuel and maintenance costs are to be borne by public funds, to avoid administrative accountability and legal strictures, the plates themselves are artificially altered. (Time expired.)
Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Member Roshni Meche.
(12:26 PM)
Honorable Member Roshni Meche (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Honorable Chairman,
(12:26 PM)
Sir, the government is trying to impose restrictions on student union elections in universities, stating that university students should not engage in politics. However, children under 18 are made members of their own affiliated political parties. What kind of double standard is this? Section 14, Sub-section 2(a) of the Political Parties Act, 2073 BS, clearly states that one must have completed 18 years of age to become a party member. In Nepal, children under 18 are barred from voting. But who gave the RSP the right to make children ineligible to vote party members? Does this party not fall under Nepal's laws? Is it exempt from acting in accordance with Nepal's Constitution and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child? The government, which lacks even the basic understanding that student unions and political parties are different, seeks to bar students from student unions in universities, stating that students should not engage in politics or express their views, but children should be made to carry the flag of their affiliated party. (Time expired.)
Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Member Basudev Ghimire.
(12:28 PM)
Honorable Member Basudev Ghimire (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairman, the future of students in grade 12 is being ruined by the mistake and erroneous decision made by the Ministry of Education and the Minister of Education. In such a situation, through you, Honorable Chairman, I want to ask the Honorable Prime Minister: what action will be taken against the Minister of Education? Thank you, Jai Nepal.
Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Member Samjhana Devkota.
(12:28 PM)
Honorable Member Samjhana Devkota (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Honorable
(12:28 PM)
Chairman, although Gorkha is nearby, it is a Himalayan region. Both Chumanubri and Samagaun in Gorkha have borders with China. The border at Mullabhanyang in Chhekampar is also a trade center, from where one can reach Mullabhanyang in Tibet, China, in just 6-7 hours of walking. However, that border is not open yet, making it difficult for the people of Chhekampar to make a living by bringing in trade goods. While a tourist route permit is currently given only up to Gumba in Chumanubri, the border at Mullabhanyang should be opened. By extending the tourist path to the beautiful valley of Cholpa Lake, it will be easier to trade in the beautiful lakes, mountains, and herbs found there. Therefore, the border from Sidhiwas to Chheket and up to Chhekampar should be opened. (Time expired.)
Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Member Somnath Poudel.
(12:29 PM)
Honorable Member Somnath Poudel (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Honorable
(12:30 PM)
Chairman, the export of areca nuts has been banned since August 2079 BS, and they cannot be exported. There is a significant areca nut cultivation in Jhapa, with an annual production of about 15,000 metric tons. On August 13, 2079 BS, the Development, Economic Affairs, and Good Governance Committee of our National Assembly directed that areca nuts should only be exported after DNA testing. However, the government has not established a DNA testing laboratory as per the directive, leading to the halt in areca nut exports. The farmers' areca nuts are on the verge of spoiling. Therefore, I want to draw the government's serious attention to this. The government has not only failed to establish a laboratory for DNA testing but has not done so yet. Therefore, through you, Honorable Chairman, I urge the committee to immediately withdraw this decision and provide relief to the farmers. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable members, the Zero Hour session concludes here.
(12:31 PM)
I will provide time for honorable members to speak. First, Honorable Member Durga Gurung, time 10 minutes. Following this, Honorable Member Nar Bahadur Bista.
Honorable Member Durga Gurung (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairman, today is Ashad
(12:31 PM)
15, National Paddy Day and the day for eating curd and beaten rice. I extend my heartfelt greetings to all the farmer brothers and sisters on this occasion. Paddy, which yields a mound from a handful sown, is a symbol of the hard work, sacrifice, and productivity of Nepali farmers. In Nepal, an agricultural country, paddy is not just a crop; it is an important foundation connected to our economy, culture, and lifestyle. But it is a tragedy that even today, farmers face shortages of fertilizer, seeds, irrigation, technology, and markets. Agricultural development is impossible without ensuring fair prices for farmers' labor. On this occasion, I urge the government to bring more effective programs for farmer-friendly policies, agricultural modernization, fair prices for produce, and food security assurance. Expressing high respect for the country's backbone, the farmer, I extend my best wishes.
Honorable Chairman, today, through this esteemed house, I wish to raise an extremely serious and sensitive issue concerning landless squatters, unorganized settlers, single women, disabled citizens, Dalits, senior citizens, children, and marginalized communities across the country. Today, incidents of forced eviction, house demolitions, and pushing citizens onto the streets without alternative arrangements are increasing in various parts of the country. Disregarding the human sentiments of citizens in the name of development is unbecoming of any democratic state, Honorable Chairman. The constitution guarantees every citizen the right to live with dignity, the right to housing, social justice, and social security. But what do we see in practice? Solutions are not sought, dialogues are not held, and rehabilitation arrangements are not made before the bulldozers roll. Pain is seen only after houses are demolished; this situation is extremely tragic. I ask the government: what justice is the state practicing by demolishing the roofs over the heads of single women? In which provision of the constitution is forcing disabled persons, senior citizens, Dalits, and children to live under the open sky consistent? How does the government consider evictions carried out without arrangements for alternative housing, rehabilitation, and livelihoods as just?
Honorable Chairman, landless and squatter citizens are not the enemies of the state; they are also citizens of this country. Treating them like criminals is not a solution; the basis for problem-solving should be a systematic legal process, just rehabilitation, and humane treatment. Therefore, I strongly demand from the government that no citizen should be evicted without arrangements for alternative rehabilitation. Landless and unorganized settlers...

Do not do it. Identify the landless and expedite the work of land management. Special protection and rehabilitation arrangements should be made for single women, persons with disabilities, Dalits, senior citizens, and families with children. A long-term land management policy should be implemented in coordination with local, provincial, and federal governments. Problems should be resolved not by force, but on the basis of dialogue, consensus, and social justice.

Honorable Chairperson, who is most affected when a house collapses? Children going to school are not able to attend school regularly today. Their books, notebooks, uniforms, and learning environment have all been destroyed. Their future is uncertain. Chronic patients have lost their regular medications, and some have been deprived of treatment. They have reached a point where they cannot even take life-saving medicines on time. Single women are forced to spend nights under the open sky with their young children in their arms. Senior citizens are forced to wander in search of safe shelter in the twilight of their lives. The situation is even more difficult for citizens with disabilities. Honorable Chairperson, is this social justice? Is this the right to live with dignity guaranteed by the constitution? Is development only possible by demolishing the houses of the poor? I want to tell the government clearly: bulldozers can demolish houses, but the state does not have the right to demolish the hopes and trust of its citizens. Therefore, I strongly demand from the government that arrangements be made for the immediate resumption of children's education. Immediate health services and medicines should be arranged for chronic patients, pregnant women, persons with disabilities, and senior citizens.

The most affected are Dalits, the poor, single women, senior citizens, persons with disabilities, and working-class people. Their problems are not just about land; they are related to education, health, drinking water, employment, and a dignified life. Data has been collected, but citizens have not yet received land allocation and assurance of local residence. Honorable Chairperson, a state that cannot wipe the tears of the poor, landless, and marginalized citizens cannot be a democratic and just state. Therefore, this issue should not be treated merely as an administrative process, but as a matter of human rights, social justice, and citizen dignity, and the government should take immediate steps for its resolution.

Honorable Chairperson, today I want to draw the government's attention to a very serious and sensitive issue. The primary responsibility of any democratic state is to protect the lives, education, and dignity of its citizens, especially children. The Constitution of Nepal has granted children the fundamental right to be free from violence, exploitation, and abuse. Nepal has also made international commitments to protect child rights. However, recent developments raise a serious question as to whether the state has been successful in fulfilling this responsibility. If the education, health, safety, or dignity of children has been adversely affected due to the negligent actions or carelessness of state bodies, the government cannot evade responsibility, Honorable Chairperson. Any infringement on the human rights of children is unacceptable.

No one is above the law. Whether it is a party in government or the opposition, state bodies, or any other institution, all must be within the equal purview of the law. Therefore, an impartial, independent, and transparent investigation into this incident must be conducted, and anyone found guilty must be punished according to the law. I want to ask the Government of Nepal clearly: What investigation has the government conducted into this incident? What steps have been taken to protect the rights of the victimized children? What action plan has the government made to bring the culprits to justice, and what institutional reforms are being made to prevent such incidents from recurring in the future?

Honorable Chairperson, children's tears should not be politicized. Their future, safety, and rights must be above the interests of any party, government, or individual. Therefore, I strongly demand from the government that the truth of this incident be made public, justice be ensured for the victims, and the culprits, whoever they may be, be punished according to the law. This is the true test of democracy, the spirit of the constitution, and the rule of law. Thank you. Jai Nepal.

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Nar Bahadur Bista, time 10 minutes.
(12:40 PM)
After this, Honorable Member Samjhana Devkota.
Honorable Mr. Nar Bahadur Bista (Communist Party of Nepal): Honorable Chairperson
(12:41 PM)
Sir, first of all, I would like to extend my heartfelt greetings to all the farmers of Nepal on the occasion of Asar 15, National Paddy Day. I hope you will try to produce a lot of paddy. I have a small song, a song that has recently gone viral on social media. The song is very poignant:

"Your party is built on conspiracy,
The blood of the poor has flowed due to your oppression.
Killing the poor, putting the country at stake.
Your hunger will not be satisfied by the borrowed loan, the loan shark's cooperative will not cover your shame.
Putting the country and the people at risk, burning Nepal in the name of the youth.
Searching for proof of border encroachment by neighboring countries."

This is the background of this government. The convention of Rastriya Swatantra Party was held, and only 18 out of 4900 representatives voted. In the Finance Minister's document, it is stated that the provincial assembly will be abolished. The Chairperson's document mentions restructuring. Is this party really trying to split into two factions? Because of the conspiracy in this convention, even its own members, not just me, but honorable members themselves have reacted by saying that those who should have been able to vote could not vote, and even the candidate himself could not vote for himself, such discussions are widespread. Therefore, looking at this government, it seems that not only the government but also the party is leaning towards fascism. It is putting the country at risk, and today it is also failing diplomatically. You just heard that Germany has sternly summoned Nepal's ambassador regarding the MRP issue and given its reaction.

On one hand, the country is in a dire situation with high inflation and no price monitoring. Farmers are suffering, unable to get fertilizer and seeds. Students are suffering, unable to get books. We talk about good governance. We never tire of talking about good governance. But I see the Prime Minister's Office acting like Hitler's gas chamber in Germany, calling heads of constitutional bodies and abusing them, calling human rights activists and abusing them, threatening them, intimidating them. The Prime Minister himself is the Defense Minister. But the Army Chief comes to meet the Defense Minister, talks for three hours, and then leaves. If the government, the Prime Minister, is building the country, it is brought out. Where is the country being built, what is being built, neither the media knows, nor its party's honorable members know, nor the public knows. What is being built in the Prime Minister's Office in Singha Durbar? Is it a decree being made there? Because no one knows what is happening inside. It will not come out. It is mysterious. Perhaps the current Prime Minister of our country, with a two-thirds majority, sitting mysteriously, makes the public anxious. He has no diplomatic moves, no political agenda on how to proceed with Nepal's political parties, nor any plan on how to solve the daily problems of the people. But suddenly, our Prime Minister, not just India, but Nepal also claims that India has encroached on our border, and he rushes off again. Now, there is also a fear that Nepal has stopped Indian tea, and India has also stopped Nepali tea, but this government does not care. Because this government is so helpless that it demolishes settlements with bulldozers, but then issues directives to leave the slum areas within a few hours.

On the other hand, the country was burned and destroyed. Thousands of vehicles, including vehicles inside Singha Durbar, were burned, but today a news is coming out. They are buying vehicles worth 3 billion. At least I tell the Honorable Prime Minister, Honorable Home Minister, go and see those vehicles inside the old Parliament building once. When are you going to inspect them?

The Finance Minister is bringing a report saying the provincial assembly is a burden. On the other hand, 57 ministers are being wasted, and yet they talk about good governance. They create positions that do not exist and decide from the cabinet to have nine Deputy Prime Ministers. There are no Deputy Prime Ministers, so why are nine Deputy Prime Ministers needed? On one hand, they incite people by saying that old parties have eaten this country, and on the other hand, they are ruining their own country. We need to be vigilant about the conspiracy against the constitution, creating a vortex in this country. Is there an attempt and conspiracy to nullify the constitution, which was achieved through the sacrifices of thousands, in 2072 BS? There are talks of abolishing the press, and on the other hand, by doing various other things, throwing the country into a pit and bringing it into instability, declaring this country a failed state, I strongly condemn the efforts being made by this government, this two-thirds majority government. All of us Nepalis need to be vigilant. Will the arrogance of the two-thirds majority ever throw this country into a pit and declare it a failed state? This question arises in the minds of every Nepali today.

On the other hand, they talk about good governance and corruption. Today, the Vice-Chancellors of universities are taking interviews. Each Vice-Chancellor is appointing separate people from the Prime Minister and the Education Minister for each position, asking how much they will pay. Is this good governance? Today, universities are in disarray. Schools are in disarray. They talk about good governance. Therefore, through you, Honorable Chairperson, I want to draw the government's attention that this country will not be built by writing statuses or abusing any party. To build this country, dialogue is needed, political dialogue is needed, diplomatic dialogue is needed, and only then can a blueprint be drawn on how to transform the face of this country. But we see that outside, the speeches of the honorable members in the House of Representatives and such amusing things also come out on social media that honorable members do not even recognize their own Speaker, calling them 'Sir' or 'Madam'. Looking at this, this government should learn a lesson about what kind of people have been made into what. One honorable member said in the house that we need to be allocated a budget. That seems right because they need to be trained, right? Spending state money. I suggest that you do a little of that. We don't need it, we are already self-sufficient. Therefore, here, in front of our college, our student brothers and sisters have come. The Rastriya Swatantra Party, which bans students, gives party membership to 35,000 students under 18 from its convention. What kind of party is this? What party is this? What caste is this party made of? No one knows. Therefore, there are no words to describe this party.

Therefore, in conclusion, I want to say that the country should not be plunged into conflict in the name of good governance, and we express our commitment to always remain firm in protecting the constitution, concluding my remarks. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Samjhana Devkota, time 8 minutes.
(12:59 PM)
After this, Honorable Member Mohammad Khalid.
Honorable Ms. Samjhana Devkota (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honorable

(12:52 PM) Mr. Speaker, today is Ashar 15, the 23rd National Paddy Day. The government is celebrating Paddy Day with the slogan "Climate-Friendly Technology, Self-Reliance in Paddy, and Prosperity." We are self-reliant in paddy, but dependent on others for seeds. Therefore, I request the government, which is importing paddy seeds worth approximately 1.5 billion rupees, to become self-reliant in paddy seeds from the upcoming year, and I extend my best wishes to all farmers.
Today, we are also facing an extreme shortage and price hike of petroleum products. Due to the war in the Middle East, waterways have also been obstructed. Due to the war in these countries, the price of petroleum products has increased extremely in the international market. The price of crude oil in the international market increased from 76 US dollars per barrel to 110 US dollars per barrel. Due to this war, we in Nepal are also facing an extreme shortage and extreme price hike of petroleum products. The government has increased prices five times from May 2083 BS to the present. Diesel and kerosene have increased from 142 to 237 rupees per liter, approximately 67 percent. Petrol from 157 to 219 rupees, approximately 39 percent. Aviation fuel from 127 to 269 rupees, approximately 24 percent. Currently, the price of diesel and kerosene remains the same as of today. Therefore, I want to draw the government's attention to how it will adjust this price, which has reached its highest point.
Honorable Speaker, currently, with the progress of peace in the Middle East, the price of oil in the international market has decreased to 69/70 dollars per barrel, which is lower than before. The price of refined oil has also decreased proportionally. While the price of oil is decreasing in neighboring countries, the government in Nepal is maintaining the same price. The government is not adjusting the price. I want to ask the government, where is this government's attention going? Why is it not paying attention to the livelihood of the people? I want to draw the government's attention to the fact that as the price decreases in the market, the same should happen in Nepal. The government should implement automatic price adjustments for petroleum products. Alternative routes for the import of petroleum products should be explored. Nepal Oil Corporation should be monitored at a high level, along with the monitoring of all markets. Work on petroleum exploration in Dailekh should be expedited.
Mr. Speaker, in this context, I would like to add another issue. When swimming, bathing, or crossing rivers, many children and people have lost their lives. Per one hundred thousand people, 5.4 people, approximately 1600 people annually, die due to drowning for various reasons related to water. Today alone, news has come that two children drowned and died in the Bagmati River in Gadhimai, Rautahat, while bathing and swimming. Nepal ranks among the top 10 countries in Asia for drowning deaths. According to Nepal Police data from the last three years, 2,405 people have died from drowning in Nepal. Looking at the provincial data, Lumbini Province has 501, Madhesh Province has 499, Koshi Province has 461, Karnali Province has 456, Bagmati Province has 334, and other provinces also have similarly alarming data. Approximately 80 percent of those who die from drowning are children under 24 years old. Drowning is the third leading cause of death for children aged 5 to 10 years. I want to draw the government's attention that the number of children dying from drowning can be reduced by approximately 8 percent if we pay attention. I want to request local municipalities and wards to mark high-risk areas of rivers and streams and areas suitable for swimming. The government should ensure that local police monitor and patrol risk areas. Swimming should be taught in secondary education, and students should be given certificates. Potholes in roads and under-construction structures must be filled in time. Local wards should conduct interaction programs to inform children and parents. We can also use these rivers and streams in a multi-dimensional way to save human lives. We can connect ponds and lakes with adventure sports and promote them as tourist areas. Nepal is very suitable for developing various types of sports as tourist attractions, and the rivers and streams provide a favorable environment for this. I want to draw the government's attention to giving special attention to various tourist sports, other sports, and swimming.
93 Mr. Speaker, at this time, during the rainy season, just as the rain pours down on the settlements of the landless, tears are continuously falling from the eyes of the landless. They are being ordered to leave the holding centers immediately. How can the landless be managed if they are forced to leave the holding centers after paying 24,000 rupees? Today, the unmanaged, landless squatters are struggling to find shelter. I want to draw the government's attention to this. The government's behavior towards the squatters, disregarding the fundamental rights guaranteed by the constitution, is inhumane. The work being done by this government is of such a low standard that it cannot be compared to any other. I want to draw the government's attention to immediately solve the landless problem and arrange for their proper housing, rather than forcing them to leave the holding centers. At this time of the rainy season, if our own houses leak and we cannot protect them from floods and rainwater, how will those helpless squatters survive? There are not only young people there, but also the elderly, new mothers, women, children, and disabled people. It is the government's duty to protect those disabled and vulnerable children. The government's ministers are present here. Through the ministers and the honorable Speaker, I want to draw the government's attention to immediately solve the landless problem and arrange for them to be housed properly, rather than leaving the holding centers. Because the government is the guardian. A guardian cannot abandon their guardianship. The government is neglecting its duties and wandering around. The government's attention is not on the people; the government's attention is diverted elsewhere, lost in politics. I urge the government to return to its duties, to protect Nepal and its people, and to protect the people as the primary responsibility, to protect the livelihood of the people as the first task. I want to draw the government's attention through the honorable Speaker to focus on these tasks. Thank you.
Honorable Speaker: Honorable Member Mohammad Khalid, time 5 minutes.
(12:59 PM) After this, Honorable Member Bishnu Kumari Sapkota.
Honorable Mr. Mohammad Khalid (JSPN): Honorable Speaker,
(1:00 PM) The monsoon has arrived, and today is also Ashar 15. I want to draw attention to two matters related to the rainy season. Firstly, I have spoken about the Kamala bridge connecting Siraha and Dhanusha in this house many times. Other members have also raised this issue. Like previous governments, this government has also not listened to this matter. The current situation is that two districts are completely disconnected. The concerned body had awarded a contract for a temporary diversion at a cost of several crores, but that has also been washed away. My humble request is that the government consider some alternative, even if it's just for bicycles and motorcycles.
I have heard about removing squatters from holding centers. Their arrangements should have been made even before their houses were demolished. The pain of being thrown out of one's home is known to the homeless. I am reminded of a verse by Bashir Badr:
"It takes a lifetime to build a home,
And you show no mercy in burning down settlements."
Honorable Speaker, federalism did not come out of anyone's mercy. The Nepali people brought federalism by fighting against the unitary system, through martyrdom, injuries, imprisonment, and facing lawsuits. There are rumors spreading that federalism is not succeeding, it is expensive, it is difficult to support hundreds of MPs, it is like raising elephants, etc., and there are discussions about weakening or abolishing federalism. After the Janmat movement, before the elections on Falgun 29th, the current honorable Prime Minister, then a senior leader of Rastriya Swatantra Party and a candidate for future Prime Minister, Balendra Shah, had gone to Janakpur and said, "Now the people of this place have to go to Kathmandu for rights, for work, for any other reason like sightseeing or other activities, you will have to go there." The people thought that whatever the previous governments could not do for federalism and for the oppressed, neglected, rejected, and excluded people of this region – Tharus, Madhesis, Janajatis, Dalits, Muslims – this son of Madhesh has come, and believing that the daughters have also come, they gave an unprecedented vote. We still have hope. Because executive power is in his hands. We still hope that the government will not go against the abolition of provincial assemblies or federalism, but rather how federalism can be strengthened, and about the rights of castes and ethnic groups in the country that have not received rights so far, which we have not fully fulfilled, there will be discussions. Rights will reach them. Today, I wish to conclude with the same hope, that this government will take steps to further strengthen federalism. Thank you.
14 Honorable Speaker: Honorable Member Bishnu Kumari Sapkota, time 14 minutes.
(1:05 PM) After this, Honorable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma.
Honorable Mr. Bishnu Kumari Sapkota (Nepali Congress): Honorable Speaker,
(1:06 PM) Today is Ashar 15, we have a tradition of "planting a handful and harvesting a mound." Today is National Paddy Day. I am reminded of how, as the daughter of a farmer, when I grew up, my fields were surrounded by paddy fields, and this day was very enjoyable. Even when we went to school, we would sneak away from school, enter the fields, plant paddy, play folk music, play traditional instruments, sing folk songs, and have so much fun. I remember the joy of playing in the mud and planting paddy. Remembering that joy and playing in the mud, I want to extend my best wishes to all my farmer brothers and sisters on National Paddy Day.
Honorable Speaker, our country is also an agricultural country. Our country is extremely beautiful. All kinds of grains, all kinds of vegetables, and all kinds of fruits are produced in our country. We have all kinds of climates in the Himalayas, hills, and Terai. We have diverse birds and animals. Nepal is so beautiful. In the past, when we did any work and introduced ourselves, if asked "What do you do?", we would say "I am a farmer." But today, that is diminishing rapidly. The perspective towards farmers is not respectful. Today, if someone goes abroad and washes dishes or cleans floors, no matter how menial the job, they are respected when they return to Nepal. They are also given loans and other facilities. But a farmer who toils day and night in the soil and dust to produce food does not even have time to walk around proudly. They are looked down upon, and it hurts their feelings. Rather than suffering here, it is better to go abroad...

Many of our brothers and sisters, farmers, have gone abroad today. To stop this, the government must prioritize agriculture the most. But that is not being seen. It is not enough to just give subsidies to farmers. Some money is given as subsidy, and they are told to do this work, but farmers are troubled by floods, landslides, droughts, and all other things. They cannot even recover their invested capital, let alone make a profit, so how can they survive? Therefore, the government must now adopt a new policy. Despite all this, 2.6 million farmers in our country are registered in agriculture. More than 60,000 farmers are dependent on agriculture. We must not let them migrate from the country now. Arrangements should be made for training for farmers, and that training must be real training. After they go and work, it must be monitored whether they worked or not, and the government should pay attention to all three levels of government – local, provincial, and federal. Farmers should be provided with a salary at the officer level, and if they are encouraged with the profit they earn from producing more, then farmers will be able to farm in this fertile land while staying in Nepal. Today, I myself have sown mustard in my land, where three or four crops can be grown. There is arrangement for everything, but there is no manpower. Today, I am ready to give such land to anyone who wants to work and earn a living. Many people are ready, many houses in villages and districts are locked. Many sons and daughters are abroad. So, shouldn't an initiative be taken to attract them back? Yesterday, before the election, everyone used to say the same thing when asking for votes in the villages: 'We want to form a new government this time. We will vote for the bell because our sons and daughters will return!' We need to bring support for our old age back to Nepal; we are not happy going abroad and leaving our homes. So please forgive us, we were also told that if we change our vote now, we will be held accountable, but so many months have passed, why is there no arrangement? It is not enough to blame only the old political parties today. How much did the old political parties struggle? They had to go to jail, endure hardship, live without proper shelter, walk long distances, they didn't have mobile phones or vehicles, they endured so much hardship to reach villages, participated in the joys and sorrows of the citizens, understood their pain, and encouraged them to bring about democracy. They brought the workers and laborers to the streets. Today, student organizations are being banned for various reasons, and they are being stopped with various restrictions. They are the power that raises a strong voice for this nation, for democracy, for the people's democracy. Such power cannot be stopped. If students had not protested yesterday, if citizens had not gone to the streets and protested to bring about this democracy, this people's democracy, how could today's government have been formed? How could it have been formed so easily and smoothly today? Student organizations cannot be stopped today. Student union elections must be opened. The student union is a place to discuss their rights and interests. The student union is a place to understand the pain of students. Therefore, student unions cannot be stopped. Today, while discussing student unions, is the government, the largest party in the country, the largest party Rashtriya Swatantra Party, a government with nearly two-thirds majority, responsible? Can children under 18 be used? Yesterday, they used to say that the old parties used children, and today they are using them themselves? What is the difference then? The old parties might have mobilized them for a specific cause. They might have mobilized everyone on the streets. If you are also walking the same path today, then what kind of new party is this? What is new? You must be able to provide new ideas, you must show that by doing it. Today, 100 days have passed, what are the 100 works of 100 days? I want to ask for an account of the 100 works of the government's 100 days through the Honorable Speaker. And today, the citizens, the farmers are in the fields, looking up at the sky, waiting for the road, waiting for fertilizer and seeds. Yesterday, when we raised this issue in this respected house, we all loudly demanded that the government arrange for fertilizer, as the monsoon is coming, and it is time for farmers to cultivate. But the answer we received was, 'You be quiet, this government will not withhold fertilizer from the farmers for even a single minute.' If you cannot do it, why talk about it? Why give assurances? False assurances cannot last. The citizens of Nepal have scales in their hands, and those scales never tilt to one side; history is a witness. Today, the scales might have tilted towards you, your government has been formed, but what have you given to the citizens? People will not believe sweet talk and flashy words anymore. Today, how much contribution has been made to bring about this province, this federalism? How many martyrs have sacrificed their lives? How many people are displaced and homeless? How many people have lost their limbs and become disabled? Saying 'we will abolish provinces, we will abolish federalism' is easy. You must show that you can do it. Only those who have done it know. The pain of the Khukuri is known only to the chopping block. Those who have suffered know. Today, the provincial government, the local government, might have provided concessions, facilities to the citizens there. You must understand that. And then we say 'we will abolish the federal government,' 'this is not working,' 'that is not working.' You must do it first and then show it. That is why I tell the government, through you, Honorable Speaker, do only what you can do. Do not make citizens hopeless with false assurances. Yesterday, while criticizing the old parties, fingers are now being pointed at you too. Time is powerful, so no one can go ahead of time. Man is a slave to time and circumstances. Today, our अन्नदाता (providers of food) farmers have not received fertilizer, when will it be available? And after the time is up? What is the use of fertilizer given after the time has passed? If a farmer is even one day late in planting crops, if it is insufficient for just one day, that one day causes 15 days of damage to the farmer. As time passes, everything has its time, and after that time has passed, the planted crop cannot yield as expected. So how can farmers be satisfied? It is not just farmers who suffer; all of us citizens eat because farmers produce. Today, so much is happening. Today, the farmer's mind is our mind. Today, taxes are imposed on education and health. Today, fuel has become expensive due to international reasons, but we have electricity. We have abundant water; we can generate electricity. Should we give discounts on electricity or not? Today, the landless were first told that they would be given land ownership certificates and settled, but they were evicted from their settlements without prior preparation. But now they are being evicted again after being brought to the holding center. Where will they go? Can 24,000 people find accommodation in Kathmandu? Not even a single room can be found. How expensive is Kathmandu? And when such irresponsible actions are taken, the government should think once. We want this government to last for 5 years. We are tired; the country has been hollowed out by elections every 6 months, 9 months, 1 year, 2 years. We do not want to have elections again. You must last, but to last, you must behave accordingly. You must be able to coordinate with all political parties. You also fought. Today, why did you extend the convention in Chitwan by two days more than planned? It should have been by mutual understanding, shouldn't it? It turns out it wasn't. Tomorrow, the process will be the same. Therefore, if you work with restraint and thoughtfulness, you will succeed. The success of the government means the success of the country, and the success of the country means the success of the citizens. Therefore, I urge the government, through you, Honorable Speaker, to speak very thoughtfully. Do not say anything that harms the nation regarding nationalism, because you are responsible. Irresponsible people should not speak, let alone responsible people. Thank you. Presiding Officer: Honorable Vice-Chairperson Ms. Lila Kumari Bhandari. (13:12 hrs) Honorable Speaker: Honorable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma, you have 8 minutes. After this, Honorable Member Somnath Poudel. Honorable Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Nepal Communist Party): Honorable Speaker Sir, the devastating earthquake on June 10, 2026 (2083 Jestha 27) has devastated Venezuela. 1400 people have died. More than 40,000 people are missing or out of contact. Therefore, I want to offer my heartfelt condolences to all those who died in Venezuela. I wish for the speedy recovery of the injured. Speaker Sir, the National Independent Party's convention has just concluded. I want to thank them for concluding the convention. But what will the country learn from the Raswapa convention? I have found that it has created disorder. The first convention of Raswapa in Chitwan created disorder. First of all, the convention has raised the issue of abolishing provinces. Abolishing provinces or attacking federalism means attacking proportional representation, inclusivity, secularism, and the rights vested in the people. Therefore, this convention has gone against its party's electoral commitment, and this is also a kind of disorder. Bharatpur is a beautiful metropolis. The convention has made the beautiful city ugly by piling up empty bottles of liquor, beer bottles, food packets, and leftover food on the roads, squares, and fields. This is another disorder. On the other hand, everyone invites various parties to the convention. International organizations are also invited, and it is a tradition to offer suggestions and best wishes to that party. The guests present and invited guests have fulfilled their responsibilities. They offered best wishes and gave some suggestions to the party. But the leaders of that convention, the cadres who attended the convention, have insulted the guests. Guests have been branded as terrorists and corrupt. That is another disorder. Does the National Independent Party have no discipline? Are rules not applied to them? Are they not subject to discipline? If discipline is not applied at all, then they can say anything, but should Raswapa take action against such cadres or not? I demand that those chaotic cadres be punished immediately. On the other hand, cadres who received many votes but contested for the central committee are now appearing in interviews on social media, saying, 'We received many votes, but our names did not come up.' How can those who received many votes be defeated? What could be a greater disorder than that? Not only that, but these cadres and leaders are now in a situation where they have to seek judicial process, and their right to go through that judicial process can be heard. In this context, contrary to the Constitution of Nepal, contrary to international treaties and conventions, contrary to the law related to political parties in Nepal, 35,257 minors under 18 years of age have been made party members, made to carry party bags, made to carry party flags. This is another...

It is a mistake. Does the Rastriya Swatantra Party not follow rules, not follow laws, not follow international treaties and agreements? This is also a serious question. This question can arise internationally and also in the Nepali courts. There are many distortions seen in the general convention of Rastriya Swatantra Party. When will the Rastriya Swatantra Party correct these distortions?

Respected Chairperson, our learned Finance Minister brought the budget. But looking at it, listening to it, studying it, the budget brought by the Finance Minister, who is seen as a respected personality of the country, does not seem to align with Nepal's sociology and economics. I also felt that our Finance Minister has not studied Nepal's sociology and Nepal's economics. My father, a farmer from a poor family, used to say, "Son, feed the hungry, clothe the naked." The person who is suffering, the person who works all day, earns wages, toils in farming, that person is very hungry. The person who works hard is hungry. Therefore, the hungry person should be fed first, he used to say. Similarly, the person who works hard, farms, goes to the forest, brings firewood, cuts grass, raises cattle, that person's clothes also tear and get ripped frequently. Therefore, the naked person should be clothed before others who do not work and have new clothes, he used to say. This is the social and economic formula. Therefore, our Finance Minister brought the budget to support the middle class, but did not bring the budget for the hungry and naked people. Therefore, this is a proverb from Karnali, there is a proverb in Karnali, a proverb that is on people's lips, which is, "Feed the hungry, clothe the naked." Today, that is the situation in Nepal. Nepal's geography is suffering, the people are suffering, and the community is suffering. In this country made up of various castes, ethnicities, religions, and cultures, economic culture and economic development are also of various types. Therefore, it is necessary to include the hungry and naked, feed them first, bring them into development first, that community first. Thank you.

Somnath Poudel, time 7 minutes.

Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Member
(13:29 hrs)
After this, Honorable Member Ranjit Karna.

Honorable Shri Somnath Poudel (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Respected
(13:29 hrs)
Chairperson, I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude for the time. Today is National Paddy Day, Asar 15. On the occasion of this day, I would like to extend my heartfelt greetings to all the farmer brothers and sisters, the Annadatas. First of all, I would like to seek permission to draw your serious attention to an issue.

Currently, a matter is being reported on social media and in the news that the Prime Minister's advisors are calling the heads of constitutional bodies, judges, and various individuals and giving them directives. It is being reported that there are threats of murder if these directives are not followed. Who has given the Prime Minister's advisors this authority? They are recognized neither by the parliament nor by the constitution. Who has given these individuals, appointed to provide specific advice to the Prime Minister, the authority to consume national property and the money collected from the people's taxes to do this work? We want this house to be informed about what is happening. I want to condemn this and draw the serious attention of the government through the esteemed Chairperson of the government to stop this immediately.

Chairperson, I have another serious issue to raise today, which is about the government's 100-day promises, the 100 points. All the ministers of the government are busy building the country. It must be presented by number, so I seek permission to read out the first promise. The ruling party's 100-point promise made during the election, point number 1 states that the Dalit community has been suffering injustice, insult, exploitation, and exclusion for generations due to Nepal's social structure, state laws, policies, and practices. As a result, the rate and depth of poverty in this community are high. Instead of encouraging and providing opportunities to a community with special skills, capabilities, and potential, we acknowledge the reality that discriminatory treatment and structural barriers are created, causing the entire society to lag behind in the journey of skills, technology, and modernization. Accepting this historical reality, the new government will formally apologize on behalf of the Nepali state for the caste discrimination, injustice, and exclusion against the Dalit and backward communities in the Prime Minister's first address. We will move forward with more concrete legal, policy, and institutional reforms to end organizational discrimination. This is point 1 of their promise. My question is, when did the head of government apologize to the nation or this house? My question is, where is the program according to point 1 of this promise in the budget brought by this government? Where is the budget? I challenge the ministers to show me even one program for the Dalit community in this budget. Show me one program, one number, what have you brought for the Dalit community? I don't need to say much, one month does not make winter disappear, winter may come again, keeping this in mind, I urge the government and the ruling party. While saying this, I am reminded of a folk tale. A mouse had fallen into a jar of wine while being chased by a cat. Then, thinking it would drown in the wine, it pleaded with the cat, "Take me out of here, and you can eat me after I get out." The mouse promised the cat. As per the promise, the cat pulled the mouse out. The mouse ran and entered its hole. Going inside, the cat said, "Hey, I told you I would eat you, that was our promise." To this, the mouse said, "Oh, Brother Cat! When one drinks wine, one says many things, does it count to remember what was said while drunk?" The mouse said this. Now, if this is the promise of Rastriya Swatantra Party, like the promise made by the mouse while drunk, I have nothing more to say. If it is such a promise, then I have nothing more to say. If it is a promise made by a person consciously and soberly, then if point 1 of this promise, even point 7, is implemented like this, what will be the situation when you reach point 100? Therefore, I urge you to return to this promise. Now, while explaining this, the Finance Minister will again respond by saying, "What did you do in 24 years?" The question will surely arise. The Finance Minister is here, the Minister will surely tell you. A Member of Parliament named Somnath Poudel said this and that there, Minister. Now I want to explain to him that our party's respected Chairman of CPN UML, KP Sharma Oli, brought a budget last year under his leadership. In one point of that budget, it was stated that a budget of 50 crore would be allocated for the 'Bhagat Sarvajit Entrepreneurship Development Program' for the oppressed Dalit community. That budget was under the Ministry of Industry. I want to ask through the Chairperson, where has the implementation of that budget reached? I hear that about 80 percent of the budget was reallocated! I don't know if that program exists this year. You reallocate the budget allocated by the previous government. And then you make promises. I also want to explain to you that the previous government had brought a program to provide loans up to 10 lakhs without collateral for entrepreneurs from the oppressed Dalit community. Search for programs in the ministry. Not only that, the government had also brought a program to provide a reward of up to one lakh for inter-caste marriages between Dalits and non-Dalits. Not only that, today the government has built houses for 47,000, 50,000 citizens. Among them, the government had brought a program to build houses for Dalits who do not have houses. Search for these programs and see what the previous government did and what you have done? This is my question, thank you.

Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Member Ranjit Karna, time 12 minutes. After this
(13:36 hrs)
Honorable Member Rajendra Laxmi Gaire.

Honorable Shri Ranjit Karna (Nepali Congress):- Respected Chairperson, Sir,
(13:37 hrs)
"Kathmandu will become Singh Durbar, but where has our Janakpur's right gone?" This is not just a simple question about the rights of Maithili. This is the heartbeat of millions of oppressed citizens of Madhesh, Karnali, Far-West, Koshi, Bagmati, Gandaki, Lumbini, and all over. Today, I am not standing in this esteemed house just to give a simple formal speech. I stand here to voice the concerns of the common Nepalis who are struggling to preserve the system today, with the same passion that flowed yesterday for change. Therefore, I seek permission to present this address before this house, the government, and especially the esteemed Prime Minister, as a specific plea and...

Respected Chairperson, Sir, I want to remind the current Prime Minister, Shri Balendra Shah, of a past historic speech he gave on January 4th during an election campaign, standing on the sacred land of Janakpur: "The country should be made so strong that citizens do not come to Kathmandu to ask for rights, but only to visit Pashupatinath and Swayambhu." When he reached Karnali, he said, "Now the dreams of Karnali..." When he went to the Far-West, he said, "The Far-West is no longer far, we love you dearly." Today I want to ask the Respected Prime Minister, the leadership that advocated for the spirit of federalism and decentralization by reaching every corner of the country at that time, why are they silent now after reaching the seat of Singh Durbar? Why did the Rastriya Swatantra Party, the party led by him, pass a political resolution at the Chitwan convention to abolish the provincial assemblies yesterday? Advocating for strengthening provinces in Janakpur, talking about the respect of Karnali in Karnali, talking about rights in the Far-West, and then playing the game of abolishing provinces after returning to Kathmandu? This is not political stability, Chairperson, this is naked political opportunism. It is a great betrayal of the people. Saying anything to win elections, and then strangling the rights of the people after coming to power, such a trend does not strengthen democracy.

Chairperson, Sir, this system and federalism are not the whims of anyone's politics, nor are they a gift received from anyone's favor. We must not forget that this system, this federalism, has come from the sweat and blood of dozens of Nepalis. I want to explain, when the first Madhesh movement occurred, after dozens were injured, the then respected Prime Minister Girija Prasad Koirala addressed the issue of the Madhesh. After that, during the formation of the constitution by the second Constituent Assembly, the then Prime Minister, Honorable Sushil Koirala, institutionalized those issues, including federalism and inclusion. Not only that, the country was at a major point of civil war at that time. All things were handled wisely. The political forces of the Madhesh parties were outside the parliament, saying they would not accept the constitution. We held parliamentary elections under the leadership of the Nepali Congress, bringing all these forces together. At that time, the Prime Minister of Nepal was the then Sher Bahadur Deuba.

If this parliamentary electoral system had not been advanced intelligently, there would have been a great civil war in the country. Thousands would have been injured. Dozens would have been killed. Therefore, the Nepali Congress has also preserved this system and brought it forward.
The wounds of the Madhes movement have not yet healed. Where our brothers took bullets in their chests and planted the flag of identity and inclusivity in the country. Those who engage in cheap politics in the name of Dalits, Janajatis, women, and oppressed communities are saying, "The provinces are expensive. Let's abolish them." I want to ask, if the roof of the house is leaking, do we demolish the entire house? If there are weaknesses in the provincial government, let's reform them, cut expenses, manage them, and clarify responsibilities. The real problem is not federalism, but the meaningful implementation of federalism. The Civil Service Act, the Police Adjustment Act have not been moved forward yet. Employees are not being sent. Resources and means are concentrated at the center. And then they send them to a running race and blame the province if they can't run? This is political deceit, Mr. Chairman.
Mr. Chairman, the Rastriya Swatantra Party and the current government's constituents are playing a dangerous game by raising the agenda of the first elected executive Prime Minister and trying to change the basic structure of the constitution. I want to give a small example. If we survey 110 democratic countries in the world, and among the economically strong countries, when we survey countries with a parliamentary system, their per capita income is found to be: 60 percent are in a good position in federal parliamentary systems, 14 percent in presidential systems, and 26 percent in mixed systems. This is the global situation. When we look at democratic systems, countries with parliamentary systems are the most advanced. Today, I want to give a serious warning from this rostrum. Beware, Balen Ji! If an attempt is made to dismantle the fundamental pillars of the constitution in the name of political populism and cheap popularity, the country will fall into another disaster. Let's not commit the suicidal act of inviting another Madhes movement, another Dalit movement, another internal rebellion.
The public should not be forced to take to the streets again to protect their rights.
Honorable Chairman, we have a lot of work to do in the country right now. Currently, this government appears to be completely unsuccessful in terms of good governance. Even though fuel prices have decreased in the international market and petroleum products are being imported cheaply from India, the prices have not been adjusted in Nepal. Why are prices in Nepal out of control even when petroleum products from India are cheaper? The prices of daily necessities in the market have increased, with inflation reaching 7 percent. The purchasing power of ordinary citizens is declining. In the past, millions of Nepalis endured hardship and suffering, but why do people have to suffer the same hardships even with a new system and new faces in power? Even now, more than 2500 youths are forced to leave the country daily from Tribhuvan Airport due to lack of employment.
Today, not only the lower-middle class, but also the middle class are greatly affected by the current inflation. The kitchen of every Nepali household has become very expensive.
Mr. Chairman, I want to draw the attention of this parliament to the recently published "Infrastructure Sector Assessment" report by the World Bank. What does that international report clearly and harshly state? It says that the capital expenditure and return on investment in Nepal's infrastructure sector are the weakest and most disappointing in all of South Asia. We spend money, but the economic benefit the country receives from it is negligible. We have a lot of work to do in this system. Similarly, if we take just a small example of Nepal, India, China, and Vietnam, if we take a loan of 1 billion rupees from any donor agency for infrastructure development in Nepal, China, after receiving its 10 billion rupees, uses it commercially through the modern EPC (Engineering, Procurement, and Construction) model. There, the land and forest clearance are done before the state awards the contract, and the contractor prepares a modern 6-lane expressway of international standards six months ahead of schedule and can allow vehicles to drive on it.
Our neighboring country, India, through its revolutionary PM Gati Shakti digital portal, integrates six different ministries onto a single platform, completing land and forest clearance online within just three days, and establishes a world-class industrial corridor through its own hybrid annuity model. Vietnam, on the strong foundation of its revised PPP Act, 2020, attracts billions in foreign investment by providing revenue guarantees to foreign multinational companies and builds the world's most advanced electronics manufacturing hub. These countries have made laws a tool for development, not an obstacle to development. But in our Nepal, Mr. Chairman, in five years after the release of 10 billion rupees, we waste invaluable time playing a game of file-pushing, carrying files to the Forest Ministry for permission to cut a single tree, to the Ministry of Environment for environmental impact assessment report approval, and to the District Administration Office to determine land compensation. The time has come. Let us all work together to achieve economic prosperity and good governance in the country. I once again urge the current Prime Minister and the Rastriya Swatantra Party not to try to push the country into another disaster. Regarding his expressway, he has taken another turn, and I feel that due to his party, due to his decisions, the country may fall into another disaster, I have a fear. Therefore, I wish him well, I urge him, let's build this country together, all Nepalis, all political parties, saying this, thank you, Jai Nepal.

Honorable Chairman: Honorable Member Rajendra Laxmi Gaire, time 8 minutes.
(13:49)
Honorable Mr. Rajendra Laxmi Gaire (Nepal Communist Party): Honorable
(13:49)
Chairman, as we are discussing the country from various angles, the Government of Nepal, the current government, has set five guiding principles and 40 points, including good governance, economy, infrastructure, expansion of the middle class. Point number 9 mentions health insurance and social security system. Health insurance is a basic need for the Nepali people. They get health insurance by paying 35 hundred rupees, and today that health insurance has been stopped, it has been stopped since Jestha 16th. It has been almost a month. For a month now, the right of people to get medicine through health insurance, for which they have paid, has been curtailed. The government may have cut it for restructuring, but should it not bring a decision? Is it justifiable to collect people's money and not provide them with medicine? I want to draw the serious attention of the government to this matter. Health insurance must be resumed.
Secondly, the government has stated that it will complete incomplete projects in its current plan. This also includes drinking water projects. Last year, there was a drought in Madhes Province, and the government declared it a drought-stricken area. People reached there with water in tankers. But today, the people of Madhes have not always received water in tankers. What have they eaten? Therefore, since Madhes Province was declared a drought-stricken area, the government must come up with a plan and provide drinking water to every household in Madhes. It is necessary to have a special plan for Madhes Province, as it has been declared a drought-stricken area. There are problems in many places. But last year, we heard from the ministry officials that the people are not ready for cost sharing for drinking water. Even if the people are not ready for cost sharing now, we have heard that when the railway was brought, the British first gave money to the people who would ride the train. The railway has been brought to Gorakhpur, hasn't it? When the railway was brought from Gorakhpur to Sunauli, the British gave money to the people who would ride the train. Now that people have gotten used to it, they pay for the train. Therefore, the government must take responsibility for two years. Once they get used to it, people will pay for maintenance and drink that water. People will not wander around looking for well water or pond water. Therefore, what is needed is vision from the government, a plan is needed.
27
I want to draw the government's attention to this matter. This drought could cause havoc in various places, and the situation in Madhes could be even more dire. Therefore, I request the government to pay attention in time, and as long as we do not bring a plan to conserve groundwater, there will be a situation of havoc in our country. Therefore, the current government's attention has not been drawn to this, and this attention needs to be paid for the protection of the country, it is not in the plan.
I also want to say that we have said that the ministers are present here. Even if we are speaking to the ministers, we have raised our voices to improve the good work of the government and to correct the wrongdoings. Therefore, Article 54 of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the four aspects of child rights: the right to life, protection, participation, and the right to development. Article 15 of the Convention on the Rights of the Child gives the right to form organizations and participate. Therefore, our students have formed organizations, children's clubs have been formed, and that convention on the rights of the child also states that political parties cannot make children under 18 years of age members in political activities, carry party flags, or hoist flags. If the party has given membership as reported in the newspapers, then the government will be prosecuted according to the Convention on the Rights of the Child. Therefore, the concerned minister must use the weapon of the Convention on the Rights of the Child to cancel those memberships. Therefore, I want to draw the attention of the government ministers to the courage to cancel this wrong act.
I also want to say that while we are discussing various things, the talk of our country, feasts, and many other things have come up. During elections, they make popular promises that touch the hearts of the people. After winning the election and going to power, we cannot live by promises that are like a sword around our necks. Therefore, we cannot abandon the protection of the constitution and the republic, inclusivity, and the assurance of all these things for any region, class, or ethnicity left behind in Nepal. On that basis, how many of us have participated here. Therefore, we said yesterday, "No one is a stranger, be it from the Himalayas, the hills, or the plains." This was our slogan, so no one can be far away. Therefore, I want to say that although we have heard less speeches from our Finance Minister and Prime Minister in this house, we heard their speeches at their general convention. In that speech, our country's Prime Minister said that he has not walked on a local road, but on an expressway. What is this vehicle that has moved is an expressway. It is heading towards its destination.

After reaching, the brake is applied, it has been broken. A vehicle that brakes upon reaching its destination, a vehicle without brakes, when an accident will happen, who knows, one has to be careful about this too. Regarding what the Prime Minister said, we saw their general convention. The general convention they said would be three days turned out to be three times that, didn't it? The brake was applied there. It seems to be running as said, but it is not running. Therefore, the important thing is whether we advocated for the Nepali people or not. This is something connected to the feelings of the people of this country. We demolished the houses of the landless, and we housed them in shelters. Demolishing is easy. Today we are saying let's leave them. Now, where will they go? The government must guarantee their food, shelter, and clothing. The government must also look after their health and education. Today, when we hear about people dying there, should the government take moral responsibility or not? I state that the government must take responsibility. Thank you. Presiding again: Honorable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal. (13:53 hrs) Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, the speaking order in special time ends here. (13:57 hrs) Honorable members, now I provide time to the Honorable Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle to present the "Appropriation Bill, 2083" before the assembly in accordance with Sub-rule 2 of Rule 133 (A) of the National Assembly Rules, 2075. Honorable Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle: Honorable Chairperson, it has become necessary to present this bill to grant the authority to spend funds from the Federal Consolidated Fund for the services and works of the fiscal year 2083/084 and to appropriate that amount. The presented bill provides the authority to spend from the Federal Consolidated Fund and the provision to appropriate for the services and works to be carried out by various bodies. This bill has been presented to the Federal Parliament as a financial bill. Honorable Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I present the "Appropriation Bill, 2083" to this esteemed assembly in accordance with Sub-rule 2 of Rule 133 (A) of the National Assembly Rules, 2075. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, the next meeting of the National Assembly will be held today, 30 minutes later. This meeting is adjourned here. sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker urged the government to expedite land management for the landless, provide special protection for vulnerable groups, and implement a long-term land policy based on dialogue and social justice. They highlighted the plight of children, the sick, single women, and the elderly due to house demolitions and called for immediate resumption of education and healthcare services for affected populations.

speakers.name: Honorable Chairperson
speakers.topic: Presiding over the session and allocating time

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker emphasized that a state unable to address the suffering of the poor and marginalized is not democratic or just. They called for the land issue to be treated as a matter of human rights and dignity, not just administrative process. The speaker also raised concerns about the state's failure to protect children's rights, questioning its commitment to constitutional guarantees and international obligations.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker demanded an impartial investigation into an incident affecting children, urging accountability for those responsible and institutional reforms to prevent recurrence. They stressed that children's rights are paramount and should not be politicized, calling for transparency, justice for victims, and legal action against culprits as a test of democracy and rule of law.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Nar Bahadur Bista extended greetings on National Paddy Day and recited a song critical of the government and the Rastriya Swatantra Party, alleging conspiracy, oppression, and financial mismanagement. He questioned the party's internal democracy and its alleged leanings towards fascism and diplomatic failures, citing the MRP issue with Germany.

speakers.name: Honorable Chairperson
speakers.topic: Allocating time to the next speaker

speakers.name: Nar Bahadur Bista
speakers.topic: Criticism of government and Rastriya Swatantra Party

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker described the country's dire situation with inflation, lack of price monitoring, and suffering farmers and students. They criticized the Prime Minister's Office for alleged intimidation of constitutional body heads and human rights activists, contrasting it with the Prime Minister's own actions. The speaker questioned the government's direction and transparency, highlighting diplomatic failures and the controversial purchase of vehicles.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker criticized the government's creation of nine Deputy Prime Minister positions despite their absence, and the alleged waste of resources. They condemned attempts to undermine the constitution and warned against declaring the country a failed state. The speaker also raised concerns about corruption in university appointments and the disarray in educational institutions, advocating for dialogue to solve national problems.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker criticized the Rastriya Swatantra Party for its contradictory stance on student participation and its alleged lack of clarity. They urged the government not to disrupt the country in the name of good governance and reaffirmed commitment to the constitution. The speaker concluded by emphasizing the need for dialogue and political consensus to improve the nation's future.

sections.name: Opening
sections.summary_en: The session began with the Speaker acknowledging Ashar 15, the National Paddy Day, and its slogan. The speaker highlighted the issue of Nepal's dependence on imported paddy seeds and urged self-reliance. The discussion then shifted to the severe shortage and price hike of petroleum products, attributing it to the war in the Middle East and detailing the price increases implemented by the government.

speakers.topic: National Paddy Day and seed self-reliance
Petroleum product shortage and price hike

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker noted that international oil prices have decreased, yet Nepal's prices remain high, urging the government to adjust them and explore alternative import routes. The discussion then moved to the alarming rate of drowning deaths in Nepal, particularly among children, and proposed measures like marking risky areas, police patrols, and swimming education. The speaker also raised concerns about the plight of landless squatters, criticizing the government's actions and demanding proper housing arrangements.

speakers.topic: Petroleum price adjustment and alternative imports
Drowning deaths and prevention measures
Landless squatters' issues and housing

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Mohammad Khalid spoke about the Kamala bridge connecting Siraha and Dhanusha, which remains disconnected, urging the government to consider alternatives. He also addressed the issue of removing squatters from holding centers, emphasizing the need for prior arrangements. He then passionately defended federalism, stating it was achieved through struggle and criticizing attempts to weaken or abolish it, referencing a past statement by the current Prime Minister.

speakers.name: Mohammed Khalid
speakers.topic: Kamala bridge and squatter issues

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Bishnu Kumari Sapkota, recalling her childhood as a farmer's daughter, extended greetings on National Paddy Day, reminiscing about the joy of transplanting paddy. She then spoke about Nepal being an agricultural country with diverse produce and beautiful landscapes, lamenting the declining respect and recognition for farmers compared to those working abroad.

speakers.topic: National Paddy Day and farmers' respect

They also criticized the government's unfulfilled promises and highlighted issues with student organizations and the use of minors in politics. The member questioned the government's 100-day performance and demanded accountability.

He also criticizes the government's budget for failing to implement its promise to apologize to and uplift the Dalit community, challenging ministers to show any programs for them.
